content.title: March Madness 2026 schedule for today (3/26): Sweet 16 NCAA tournament free live streams
content.text: Updated: Mar. 26, 2026, 7:07 a.m.Published: Mar. 26, 2026, 7:07 a.m.A Houston fan dances during the first half of a NCAA tournament college basketball game. (AP File Photo/Nate Billings)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Tim Brown | The Oregonian/OregonLiveThe 2026 NCAA men’s college basketball tournament resumes with the Sweet 16 round of March Madness games getting underway today. Who will move on to the Elite 8? Get a look at the official start times and TV details for every matchup taking place on Thursday, March 26 and beyond.What is the schedule for the rest of the 2026 NCAA Tournament?Thursday, March 26: Sweet 16 Day 1(2) Purdue vs. (11) Texas | 4:10 p.m. PT | CBS(4) Nebraska vs. (9) Iowa | 4:30 p.m. PT | TBS/truTV(1) Arizona vs. (4) Arkansas | 6:45 p.m. PT | CBS(2) Houston vs. (3) Illinois | 7:05 p.m. PT | TBS/truTVFriday, March 27: Sweet 16 Day 2(1) Duke vs. (5) St. John’s | 4:10 p.m. PT | CBS(1) Michigan vs. (4) Alabama | 4:35 p.m. PT | TBS/truTV(2) UConn vs. (3) Michigan State | 6:45 p.m. PT | CBS(2) Iowa State vs. (6) Tennessee | 7:10 p.m. PT | TBS/truTVWhen and where does the 2026 Final Four take place?And here are some important dates for the rest of the 2026 NCAA men’s basketball tournament:Elite Eight: Saturday, March 28 and Sunday, March 29Final Four: 6 p.m. and 8:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, April 4 on TBS at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis.NCAA championship game: 8:30 p.m. ET on Monday, April 6 on TBS at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis.How can I watch March Madness basketball games streaming free?If you don’t have cable and just want the cheapest possible way to watch all of March Madness this year, here’s a look at the best ways to watch all of the NCAA Tournament over the next couple of weeks.The quickest and easiest way to watch this week’s games live for free is with DIRECTV (free trial).The second best option: Sling is the cheapest way to watch every NCAA tournament game (costs under $25 for the first month) except those being broadcast on CBS. However, if your TV doesn’t already have one built in, you can get an HDTV antenna to pair with your Sling subscription in order to get the games being broadcast on your local CBS station as well.If you don’t have time to order a HDTV antenna, another way to see all games broadcast on CBS is by signing up for Paramount+. This way you will be able to watch every game broadcast on CBS up through the Elite Eight. Paramount+ costs just $12.99/month and you can use it to watch on your smart TV, phone, or tablet. If you already have cable, use your login information to watch every NCAA Tournament game live through the March Madness Live app when you sign in with your cable provider login information.
